title: So glad I caught the final week of Duke & Roya #offbroadway #theatrer...
transcript: I spontaneously bought a ticket to Duke and Roya last night and then this morning they announced that it was tragically cutting its run early and closing on Saturday I'm so glad I was able to catch this and I'm really sad that you only have a few more days to see it at the Lucille Lortel Duke and Roya is an unlikely love story between Duke played by Jay Ellis who's an American hip hop star who goes to Kabul to perform on a military base and while he's there he meets Roya played by Stephanie Nur who's a uh interpreter that works on the base but Duke and Roya is so much more than just this romance it explored a lot of the differences between the cultures of both of these characters there was a lot of exploration of gender politics specifically in Kabul that I was not expecting and really appreciated also I had no idea Duke and Roy is not a two person play and in fact that the cast is rounded out by the incredible Dariush Kashani and two time Olivier Award winning Noma Dumezweni why did nobody tell me this I would have gone way sooner like the cast overall absolutely incredible the story is very simple but I was engaged the entire time my only real criticism about this show is that there were times where I was watching it and going is theatre the best medium for this story I almost wanted it to expand out into a limited series where we really got to explore these characters over the years or at the very least make it into a movie and I think part of that is because all of the scenes were almost directed like they were scenes in a film we had full on blackouts and you know I don't always love a blackout and they didn't always work for me here there were these really great concert sequences for like the first half where Jay Ellis was performing for us and the audience was just like not as engaged as I felt like they needed to be for that to truly work in a theatre medium and maybe I just was at a bad audience It was a little moments like that where I did wonder could this story be better told in a different medium and I don't necessarily know if theatre is the right medium for it I also felt like while I really enjoyed the story and the journey that it took me on that it kind of didn't know how to end and I didn't love the ending but I really enjoyed the experience of seeing this overall but Duke and Roya does two aspects of what it wants to do very well which is it has a strong core romance and it does a great job of exploring the cultures that are at play here that are kind of keeping that romance from just automatically working which I think is a great strong base for a story as far as tickets go like I said I got mine yesterday through tdF they also have a TodayTix rush this is also play at the Lortel which if you've followed me for a while you'll know they made my top 10 biggest disappointments of a theatre last year because of how bad the sight lines are in the mezzanine but I will say tonight I sat in the front row and the front row in this theatre perfect you get leg room you get a really low stage so you're not leaning your head all the way back and yes I did get to sing into the mic during one of the concert sequences would highly recommend oh there goes my light would highly recommend The Front Row for any show at the Lortel but especially this if you're going to go see it in the last couple days if you love a good Romeo and Juliet from different worlds romance with a little bit of suspense thrown in there definitely go see this I'm glad I did it's it's not the most groundbreaking piece of theatre but it was it was the perfect way for me to spend this night
